What's wrong with Vega? Besides crypto mining

Vega is basically a compute card that does graphics as a side gig. Its designed to sit inside a rack with constant high volumes of air being blown across it and doing workloads where you couldn't care less about the power consumption as long as it chews its way though the problem as fast as possible. Its something AMD GPU's have been edging closer and closer towards since the first GCN cards came out. Its not a bad gaming GPU its just not doing enough right to really put it on anyones radar right now.

Because its gaming performance isn't great AMD have had to push the stock clock as high as feasible to eek a little more performance out of the design. The end result is the Vega56 being slightly more expense and only a little bit faster in places than the closest offering from Nvidia (the 1070) and the Vega64 which only just about holds pace with a 1080 all while using considerably more power. As far as a lot of peoples opinions of AMD's Radeon brand is hot and power hungry, they can't escape this hot and power hungry stigma because they just aren't putting out competitive graphics cards right now.

Vega isn't just a problem child, its been a problem AMD have had since the Hawaii 290x and continued all the way though their Fiji, Polaris, and new Vega lines. I have had a 280x since 2013 and its been easily one of the best value for money graphics cards I've ever seen but its age is catching up on it and its energy consumption is no longer tolerable. Something like a silicon lottery 580 would be fine if I could get one at the MSRP (which I was saving for until the mining rush) but something about as fast as a Vega56 would be ideal because I could overspec for a 1080p display (maybe upscale) and get a longer useful lifetime from the graphics card, only thing is I don't want to replace what I call a power hungry GPU with another power hungry GPU so I've been caught waiting for AMD to get it right and I think I've been waiting too long.

Nvidia gpus aren't that much different in how they are designed only Nvidia has a software scheduler that can be tweaked on a case by case basis to maximize the workloads and efficiency. Its basically the driver doing more than relaying and processing commands its actually changing the workload so that very heavy workloads can be most efficiently broken into manageable jobs and if lets say the calculations go on too long the scheduler can replace that job, end it prematurely, substitute it for something more efficient with a similar result. Nvidia can use this to optimize drivers for a game very quickly and uses it to terrible effect on AMD gpus because Nvidia drivers can stop runaway wasteful computations and AMD's can't without spending time and money it doesn't have working with developers for minimal return.

AMD has had a hardware scheduler since the first GCN gpus, it occupies a big portion of the GPU die and does a lot of heavy lifting because its designed to quickly decide what jobs need to be done and what resources to allocate. Up until Polaris it was dumber than a bag of shite and needed a lot of driver jiggery pokey to stop wasting resources and more importantly time doing workloads that didn't need to be done. Thats where a portion of Polaris energy savings come from but most of its just down to the new smaller node, only thing is AMD are pushing the clock frequencies too high across all of their upper tier GPU's trying to be competitive so they end up with a hotter, higher power consumption,

AMD depended on it being the developers responsibility to optimize, Nvidia depends on how beefy a CPU you have in order to have its software scheduler catch, analyze, substitute parts of the API all the while buttering up publishers and developers with fast top shelf hardware and middleware that saves time (and money) to make sure no one really bothers with optimizing for AMD beyond ensuring it just works. Thing is Nvidia also depends on DirectX11 being horribly limiting in how workloads are processed so that Nvidias drivers can do a lot of behind the scene shit, thats why they've been pretty slow and cagey about DX12 and Vulkan where as AMD is idk, probably getting ready to shoot themselves in the foot again with some incredibly forward thinking technology that they'll just assume developers want to optimize for but really don't.
